standard_prerequisites.name: Integral closure and the definition of a normal scheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Section labelled algebra-section-normal (canonical Stacks tag 00G3); used at proof lines 14640-14641
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that for a normal scheme the ring of sections O_Y(V) of an affine open is integrally closed in its fraction field, which is the step that forces O_X(U) = O_Y(V).

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite morphism is integral, and integrality is checked on an affine open cover
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, Lemma labelled morphisms-lemma-integral-locally-finite and the definition of an integral morphism in the same chapter; used at proof lines 14641-14643
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that every element of O_X(U) is integral over O_Y(V), i.e. lies in the integral closure of O_Y(V).

standard_prerequisites.name: A birational morphism of integral schemes is an isomorphism over a dense open, so the induced map on function fields is an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, Section labelled morphisms-section-birational (canonical Stacks tag 01RJ); used at proof line 14639
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that O_Y(V) -> O_X(U) is injective and induces an isomorphism of fraction fields, so both rings sit inside one common field.

core_obligations: Reduce to an affine open V of Y whose inverse image U in X is affine, and read the morphism as an injective ring map O_Y(V) -> O_X(U) of domains inducing an isomorphism of fraction fields (proof lines 14636-14639).

Use normality of Y to identify O_Y(V) with its integral closure in the common fraction field, and integrality of f to place every element of O_X(U) inside that integral closure (proof lines 14640-14643).
Conclude O_Y(V) = O_X(U), and since V was an arbitrary affine open with affine inverse image, conclude that f is an isomorphism, i.e. that f_*O_X = O_Y (proof lines 14643-14646).
proof_roadmap: Pass to an affine open V with affine inverse image U and translate the hypotheses into properties of the ring map O_Y(V) -> O_X(U) (proof lines 14636-14639).
Insert O_Y(V) = integral closure and O_X(U) inside that integral closure, using normality of Y and integrality of f (proof lines 14640-14643).
Conclude equality of the two rings and hence that f is an isomorphism (proof lines 14643-14646).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the standard normality criterion in the relative form: a finite (or merely integral) birational morphism f : X -> Y of integral schemes with Y normal is an isomorphism (statement lines 14629-14633). The proof is short but not a citation: it has to move to an affine open V of Y whose inverse image U is affine, which is where quasi-affineness of a finite morphism is used, and then work with the ring map O_Y(V) -> O_X(U) (proof lines 14636-14639). The decisive move is to place both rings inside the same fraction field and observe that normality of Y makes O_Y(V) integrally closed there, while integrality of f puts every element of O_X(U) into that integral closure, so equality follows (proof lines 14640-14643). This is H2: the reduction to affine data and the integral-closure comparison are the non-formal content, but no Noetherian hypothesis and no descent argument are needed and the whole argument occupies a single paragraph.
